open_points.subject: Disclosure class of an empty mapped operation output
open_points.text: A07 rule 3 says a binding output takes the class the binding declares, "for the empty lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike"; A13 rule 6 says "an empty list takes the highest class among the node's inputs".
open_points.question: When a mapped operation receives an empty list, does each empty output list take the binding output port's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?
options: Use the binding output port's declared class.
Use the highest class among the node's inputs.
open_points.default_guess: Use the binding output port's declared class because A07 expressly covers this exact case.

open_points.subject: Disclosure class when a trial or execution has no inputs
open_points.text: A07 rule 3 assigns a trial case's expected output "the highest class of the case's inputs", and rule 5 defines an execution's class as "the highest class among" the inputs and, for an operation, outputs; neither phrase defines the maximum of an empty set.
open_points.question: What class is assigned to an expected output or computed execution class when the relevant input and output sets are empty?
options: Use open as the empty-set class.
Refuse inputless trial cases or executions.
Leave the class absent.
open_points.default_guess: Use open, matching A07's explicit rule for an inputless function output.

open_points.subject: Agent-originated personal data
open_points.text: State 0 says "The owner alone reads" personal data and that personal-data values "reach an agent only as digest and class", while agents may compose constants, author trial-case values, and start runs with flow-input values; A07 specifies redaction only when the surface returns values to an agent.
open_points.question: May an agent submit the full content of a value whose declared or assigned class is personal_data, or must such requests be refused or restricted to the owner?
options: Allow agents to submit full personal-data values; the restriction applies only to kernel responses.
Refuse personal-data values supplied by agents.
Permit owner submission only, requiring owner-capable variants of the affected actions.
open_points.default_guess: Allow submission and apply the restriction only to values returned by the kernel, because the action permissions otherwise provide no owner-only path for several of these inputs.

open_points.subject: Configuration-file protection during token-list reload
open_points.text: A17 rule 1 requires the configuration file to be a non-symlink regular file owned by the kernel user with no group or other permissions, but A16 rule 2 says "Exactly four checks apply to a re-read" and omits ownership, mode and regular-file checks.
open_points.question: When the configuration changes during operation, must the kernel revalidate A17's file ownership, mode and file-type requirements before accepting the new token list?
options: Revalidate all A17 file-security properties on every re-read.
Apply only A16's four re-read checks after startup.
Stop the kernel if the runtime file-security properties have changed.
open_points.default_guess: Revalidate the A17 file-security properties on every re-read and refuse requests until they pass.

open_points.subject: Credential trailing-newline handling
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 says credential content is decoded as UTF-8 "without one trailing newline" but does not define whether newline means LF only, CRLF as one newline, or any Unicode line separator.
open_points.question: Exactly which terminal byte or character sequence is removed from a credential file, and what happens when more than one such sequence is present?
options: Remove one terminal LF byte only; any remaining CR or LF is a control character and refuses the credential.
Remove one terminal LF or CRLF sequence; any additional line ending refuses the credential.
Remove one terminal Unicode line-break character or sequence.
open_points.default_guess: Remove one terminal LF, treating a preceding CR or any additional line ending as a forbidden control character.

open_points.subject: Allowed credential header value characters
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 refuses an empty credential or one containing "a control character" but neither defines control character nor specifies how other Unicode, leading whitespace or trailing whitespace is encoded and sent as an HTTP header value.
open_points.question: What exact character repertoire and byte encoding make a credential value valid for transmission as an HTTP header, and are leading or trailing whitespace allowed?
options: Require visible ASCII plus internal spaces, with no leading or trailing whitespace.
Use the HTTP client's supported header-value byte repertoire and classify unsupported values as credential_unresolved.
Encode arbitrary non-control Unicode as UTF-8 header bytes.
open_points.default_guess: Require a transport-safe visible ASCII value with no leading or trailing whitespace; otherwise return credential_unresolved.

open_points.subject: Secrets placed in manifest required headers
open_points.text: State 0 says service credentials "live in the installation's protected configuration" and never enter an answer, while A08 permits manifest instance required-header values and A10 includes those values in approval previews; no rule forbids a credential or other secret from being stored as a required-header value.
open_points.question: Must manifest required-header values be guaranteed non-secret, and if so, how is that requirement established or enforced before they are exposed in previews and responses?
options: Forbid secrets in manifest required headers as an installation/manifest obligation.
Treat required-header values as secrets and redact them like the configured credential.
Allow them to be disclosed and narrow the definition of protected service credential to the single A17 credential value.
open_points.default_guess: Declare manifest required-header values non-secret configuration and reject using them for credentials.

open_points.subject: Eligibility of an ordinary node for repeated execution
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 defines a node as ready whenever every input port holds its value, but only the mapped-node clause expressly says that a concluded element is never executed again and that waiting elements are skipped during the pass.
open_points.question: For an unmapped node whose inputs still hold values, what state excludes it from selection after it has concluded or while it waits, and under which explicit resume, approval or resolution event may it become executable again?
options: Ready also requires no concluded record and no waiting point, with explicit retry events overriding that exclusion.
Every node may be selected repeatedly while its inputs remain present.
Remove or consume input readiness after the first selection.
open_points.default_guess: Treat an unmapped node as one element: exclude it once concluded or waiting, and retry it only through the applicable resume, approval or resolution rule.

open_points.subject: Whether a waiting element can execute
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 says a mapped pass runs every element that "does not wait", while rule 7 says "A waiting element can still execute"; rules 1 and 8 otherwise describe waiting as preventing advancement until a later request.
open_points.question: Can a waiting element be selected and executed during ordinary advancement, or only when the specific approval, resolution or resume action releases or retries it?
options: Only the specific action may release or retry the waiting element.
A waiting element remains eligible during ordinary advancement.
Different waiting reasons have different eligibility.
open_points.default_guess: A waiting element is ineligible during ordinary advancement and is revisited only by its specific action.

open_points.subject: Skip versus a still-unresolved upstream branch
open_points.text: A13 rule 4 says an input that can no longer receive a value makes its node skipped_by_guard, while rule 5 says upstream_failed wins when both apply; the rules do not say whether skipping must wait for other inputs whose sources are still waiting and may later fail.
open_points.question: If one input is permanently disabled by a guard or skipped source and another input comes from a waiting source, is the node recorded skipped immediately, kept unresolved, or later changed to upstream_failed if that source fails?
options: Keep the node unresolved until all relevant upstream sources conclude, then apply upstream_failed precedence.
Record skipped_by_guard immediately because the node can never execute.
Record skipped immediately unless an upstream failure is already known.
open_points.default_guess: Keep it unresolved until the other upstream sources conclude, then record upstream_failed if any failed; otherwise record skipped_by_guard.
